description:
You are working as a penetration tester assessing a Linux system for user and permission vulnerabilities. Your goal is to enumerate all users with a login shell on the system, inspect the permissions of the /etc/passwd file, and report any users found with UID 0 other than root. 

Please perform the following steps and record your findings in a log file:

1. List all users with a valid login shell (i.e., not /usr/sbin/nologin or /bin/false) by parsing /etc/passwd.
2. Check the detailed permissions for the /etc/passwd file, including its owner and group.
3. Identify all users with UID 0 except for the root user.

Create a log file at /home/user/scan_report.log with the following format:

--- User Enumeration ---
<list of usernames, one per line>

--- /etc/passwd Permissions ---
<output of 'ls -l /etc/passwd'>

--- Non-root UID 0 Users ---
<usernames with UID 0, excluding 'root', one per line. If none, write 'None'>

The scan_report.log content must strictly match this format so it can be automatically verified.
truth:
Before the agent starts, the following conditions hold:

- /etc/passwd contains these lines relevant for the test:
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
alice:x:1000:1000:Alice:/home/alice:/bin/bash
bob:x:1001:1001:Bob:/home/bob:/usr/sbin/nologin
eve:x:1002:1002:Eve:/home/eve:/bin/sh
hacker:x:0:0:Hacker:/root:/bin/bash
service:x:1003:1003:Service:/nonexistent:/usr/sbin/nologin

- The permissions of /etc/passwd are:
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1234 Jun  1 12:34 /etc/passwd

After the agent completes the task, the file /home/user/scan_report.log must exist and have the following exact content:

--- User Enumeration ---
root
alice
eve
hacker

--- /etc/passwd Permissions ---
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 1234 Jun  1 12:34 /etc/passwd

--- Non-root UID 0 Users ---
hacker
